grammar.title: Potential complement with 懂: 聽得懂 / 看不懂
grammar.pattern: Verb (聽/看/讀) + 得/不 + 懂
grammar.explanation: To say whether you are able to understand something through listening or reading, put 得 (able) or 不 (not able) between the verb and 懂. 聽得懂 = can understand by ear; 看不懂 = can't understand by reading. The question form is 聽得懂嗎？or 聽得懂聽不懂？The object usually goes to the front: 這本書我看不懂。
grammar.contrast: 沒聽懂 vs 聽不懂: 沒聽懂 means on one particular occasion you didn't catch it (a past event — maybe he spoke too fast), while 聽不懂 means you lack the ability to understand at all. Ask yourself: one time, or in general?
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English and say 我不聽懂 or 我不能聽懂. In Chinese the 不 goes inside, between the verb and 懂: 我聽不懂.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ kàn bù dǒng.

examples.hanzi: 老師說的中文，你聽得懂嗎？
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō de Zhōngwén, nǐ tīng de dǒng ma?
examples.gloss: Can you understand the Chinese the teacher speaks?

examples.hanzi: 這個字我看得懂，可是不知道怎麼寫。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zì wǒ kàn de dǒng, kěshì bù zhīdào zěnme xiě.
examples.gloss: I can read this character, but I don't know how to write it.

passage.title: 第一天學中文
passage.hanzi: 我第一天在台灣學中文的時候，老師說的話我都聽不懂。我很想問問題，可是不知道要怎麼問。老師看到了，就笑一笑，對我說：「有問題就問，說錯也沒關係。」現在我常常第一個問老師問題，中文也比以前好多了。
passage.gloss: On my first day studying Chinese in Taiwan, I couldn't understand a word the teacher said. I really wanted to ask questions, but I didn't know how to ask. The teacher noticed, smiled, and said to me, "If you have a question, just ask — it's fine to say it wrong." Now I'm often the first to ask the teacher a question, and my Chinese is much better than before.

grammar.title: V + 完 + 再 + V：finish one thing, then do the next
grammar.explanation: 完 after a verb says the action is finished or completed. Put 再 in front of the second verb to show that the second action only happens after the first one is over: 吃完飯再看電視 = eat first, and not until then watch TV. This 再 is not 'again' here — it means 'and then'. It always goes right before the second verb, never at the end of the sentence. This pattern is very common for plans, instructions and gentle orders in daily Taiwan speech.
grammar.contrast: 先 A 再 B also means 'A first, then B', but 先…再… just orders two actions, while V完再V stresses that A must be *completed* first. If the first action has a clear end point (eat a meal, read a book, write the characters), use V完再V; if you are only listing the order, 先…再… is enough. You can also combine them: 先吃完飯再出去.
grammar.common_error: Learners say things like 我吃飯再看書 (leaving out 完) or put 再 at the end, e.g. 我吃完飯看書再. Also, 再 is for things that have not happened yet; for a repeated past action you need 又, so 我昨天再去 is wrong.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī wán wǎncān zài kàn shū.
examples.gloss: I'll read after I finish dinner.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiě wán zì zài wán diànnǎo.
examples.gloss: Finish writing the characters, then play on the computer.

examples.hanzi: 我們逛完夜市再回家，好嗎？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen guàng wán yèshì zài huí jiā, hǎo ma?
examples.gloss: Let's go home after we finish walking around the night market, okay?

grammar.title: 第 + number + 次：the nth time
grammar.pattern: 這/那 + 是 + 我 + 第 + Num + 次 + V
grammar.explanation: 次 counts times or occasions. With 第 in front of the number it means 'the nth time': 第一次 (the first time), 第三次 (the third time). The verb phrase follows directly, with no 的: 這是我第二次來台南.
grammar.contrast: Plain 次 without 第 counts how many times something happened (我去過兩次 = I've been twice), while 第…次 points to one particular occasion in the sequence.
grammar.common_error: Learners add 的 (這是我第一次的來) or say 一次 when they mean 第一次. 這是我一次來台北 is wrong; say 這是我第一次來台北.

examples.hanzi: 這是我第一次吃臭豆腐。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dì-yī cì chī chòu dòufu.

passage.title: 週末的第一件事
passage.hanzi: 週末早上，我八點就開始讀書。讀完書，我先騎腳踏車去郵局寄一個包裹，再搭捷運到台北車站和朋友見面。那是我第二次去那家麵店，麵很好吃，也很便宜。吃完飯，我們還去逛了書店。回家的時候，天開始下雨了。
passage.gloss: On Saturday morning I started studying at eight. After I finished, I first rode my bike to the post office to send a package, and then took the MRT to Taipei Main Station to meet a friend. That was my second time at that noodle shop; the noodles were tasty and cheap too. After eating, we also went to browse a bookstore. On the way home, it started to rain.

grammar.title: 因為……，所以……（because … , so …）
grammar.pattern: 因為 + 原因，所以 + 結果
grammar.explanation: Use 因為 before the reason and 所以 before the result. Unlike English, Chinese keeps BOTH words in the same sentence; it is not repetitive. You can also drop one of them (因為下雨，我沒去 / 下雨了，所以我沒去), but keeping both is the safest, most natural pattern for learners. 因為 goes at the very start of its clause, or right after the subject: 我因為不舒服，所以早點回家了。
grammar.contrast: 因為……所以…… gives a cause and its result; 但是 links two facts that clash. 我覺得很累，所以早點睡 (tired → sleep early) vs 我覺得很累，但是還要讀書 (tired, yet still must study). Ask yourself: does the second clause FOLLOW from the first (所以) or go AGAINST it (但是)?
grammar.common_error: Learners translate from English and delete 所以 (or 因為), saying things like 因為下大雨，我沒騎腳踏車 when the full pair sounds better — and, worse, they mix the pair wrongly as 因為……但是……. Another frequent slip is putting 因為 after the verb, e.g. 我沒去因為下雨, which sounds like English word order.

examples.hanzi: 因為下大雨，所以我今天沒騎腳踏車。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià dà yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ jīntiān méi qí jiǎotàchē.
examples.gloss: Because it rained hard, I didn't ride my bike today.

examples.hanzi: 因為我覺得不舒服，所以想早點回家。

passage.title: 晚上去夜市
passage.hanzi: 昨天晚上我想去夜市吃臭豆腐，但是外面下大雨，所以我沒出門。今天早上天氣很晴，我覺得下午可能不會下雨。我打電話給小明，問他要不要一起去，他說他晚上有時間。所以我們六點在捷運站見面，一起去吃臭豆腐。
passage.gloss: Last night I wanted to go to the night market for stinky tofu, but it was pouring outside, so I didn't go out. This morning the weather is clear, and I think it probably won't rain this afternoon. I called Xiaoming and asked if he wanted to come along; he said he's free in the evening. So we're meeting at the MRT station at six and going for stinky tofu together.
